question: If an AI system can rewrite its own working rules, who checks that the new rules are still good ones?
reflection: Systems that learn from their own mistakes can free people to spend more time on judgement, as long as people still set the tests.

sources.subject: AI agents rewrite their own harness to boost performance by 60%

one_line: Researchers are letting AI agents study their own failures and rewrite the software around them, which lifts smaller and cheaper models closer to the big ones.

top_stories.title: Agents that fix their own instructions
top_stories.what: A Shanghai AI lab framework called Self-Harness has an agent review its failed runs, propose new rules for itself and keep only the rules that pass regression tests.
top_stories.why: The same loop of logging failures and testing fixes is a sound method for any team that runs AI on repeated research tasks such as coding survey answers.

top_stories.title: Xiaomi open-sources a self-tuning agent toolkit
top_stories.what: Xiaomi's HarnessX treats an agent's memory, tools and control flow as swappable parts and uses reinforcement learning to search for better combinations; it reportedly lifted a small 9B model from 33% to 47% on a hard benchmark.
top_stories.why: If small models can be tuned this way, private and low-cost deployments become more realistic for organisations with strict data rules.

top_stories.title: From prompt writing to loop design
top_stories.what: The newsletter describes a shift from hand-writing prompts to designing loops with clear triggers, checks and stopping points that let agents correct themselves safely.
top_stories.why: Strong verification gates are what make automated work auditable, which matters to any public-sector or health client.

saudi_lens.text: Making smaller open models perform better on local hardware supports Saudi goals for sovereign AI and keeping sensitive data inside the Kingdom.

idea.title: Failure log for research assistants
idea.pitch: Keep a simple log of every time an AI assistant gets a research task wrong, then review it monthly to write better standing instructions.
idea.fit: Consultancy, any research team using AI
idea.first_step: Create a shared sheet with columns for task, what went wrong and the rule that would have prevented it, and fill it for one week.

idea_kids.title: Fix the robot's rules
idea_kids.pitch: A card game where children give a toy robot step-by-step rules to tidy a table, watch where it fails, and rewrite one rule each round.
idea_kids.first_step: Write eight simple instruction cards and test them with a family member acting as the robot.

terms.definition: The software around an AI model that gives it tools, memory, instructions and safety checks so it can do multi-step work.
A step-by-step record of what an AI agent did during a task, used to find where it went wrong.
A way of training AI by trial and error, rewarding the actions that lead to good results.

concepts.summary: Agents that rewrite their own operating rules from their failure logs.
Tested, automatically improved instructions let small models do more.
